questions.question: What colour are the zig-zag lines at a zebra or pelican crossing?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 uses white zig-zag lines on both sides of crossings.

questions.question: What colour are the criss-cross lines of a box junction?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 marks box junctions with yellow criss-cross lines.

questions.question: How much room should you give a cyclist when overtaking at 25 mph?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 states at least 1.5 metres at speeds up to 30 mph.

questions.question: In dry weather, what is the two-second rule used for?
options: Keeping a safe stopping gap behind the vehicle ahead
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 uses the two-second rule to keep a safe gap.

questions.question: Who needs to see your signal before you turn?
options: Other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians nearby
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 says signals warn all road users of your plans.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a signed 20 mph zone?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 requires obeying signed speed limits including 20 mph zones.

questions.question: What is the red and amber phase useful for while you wait behind the line?
options: Getting ready to move off safely once green appears
questions.explain: Rule 175: use red and amber to prepare to move off and check around you, not to cross the line early.

questions.question: What shape is a red-and-white Give Way sign?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 uses the inverted red-and-white triangle for Give Way.

questions.question: A person with a white cane is waiting at a side road you plan to turn into. What should you do?
options: Stop in good time and give way
questions.explain: Rule H2: give extra care and patience to pedestrians who may need more time to cross.

questions.question: What should you do right after checking your mirrors before changing lanes?
options: Check your blind spot over your shoulder
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do after you finish overtaking on a two-way road?
options: Move back to the left as soon as it is safe
questions.explain: Rule 160: return to the left side smoothly once you are safely past.

questions.question: What road marking sits across each entrance to a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 marks roundabout entrances with broken give-way lines.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when taking an exit to the right?
options: No signal until after you leave
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells you to signal right on approach for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: When turning right at a roundabout, what should you do with your signal before leaving?
options: Keep signalling right until you are on the new road
Switch from right signal to left signal just after the exit before yours
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states to signal left after passing the exit before your right-turn exit.

questions.question: Which blue sign warns you to keep left of a roundabout island?
options: A blue circle with white arrows pointing clockwise
A red triangle with a cross
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 explains the blue mini-roundabout and roundabout arrows showing clockwise flow.

questions.question: Where must a car driver stop on red when there is an advanced stop line?
options: Behind the first white line before the cycle box
questions.explain: Rule 178: you MUST stop at the first white line so the cycle box stays clear for cyclists.

questions.question: In Great Britain, may you turn left at a red traffic light if the road is clear?
options: No, you must wait for green
Yes, if no pedestrians are waiting
questions.explain: Rule 175: unlike some countries, there is no turn on red in Great Britain unless a green arrow shows.

questions.question: What happens if you drift sideways out of your lane on a roundabout?
options: You could collide with a car or cyclist beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns against cutting across another driver's lane when circulating.

questions.question: If the main road looks completely empty at a STOP sign, may you roll slowly through?
options: No, your wheels must stop completely first
questions.explain: Rule 171: a STOP sign is a legal MUST rule: you must come to a full standstill before moving out.

questions.question: Which approach lane should you use for an exit past straight ahead (turning right)?
options: The right-hand lane, unless signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states to use the right-hand lane when taking an exit to the right.

questions.question: You are 40 metres away at 30 mph when the light turns amber. What should you do?
options: Brake smoothly and stop behind the line
questions.explain: Rule 175: at 30 mph, 40 metres is plenty of room to stop safely behind the line.

questions.question: If there is a central refuge island on a zebra crossing, how is it treated?
questions.explain: Rule 195: a central island splits it into two separate crossings, though you should still watch carefully.

questions.question: You are two metres from the stop line at 30 mph with a car close behind when the light turns amber. What should you do?
options: Stop in the middle of the junction
questions.explain: Rule 175: you are too close to stop safely, so continuing through is the safer choice.

questions.question: Does the zig-zag no-overtaking rule apply at signal-controlled crossings like pelican crossings too?
options: Yes, it applies at all pedestrian crossings with zig-zags
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies to zebra, pelican, puffin, and toucan crossings with zig-zags.

questions.question: What should you do if a car in front stops inside a box junction and leaves no room on the far side?
options: Wait behind the box line until space opens past the box
Drive onto the yellow lines behind them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 requires waiting outside the box until your exit is clear.

questions.question: In wet or windy weather, how should you adjust your overtaking gap past a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than usual
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 advises extra clearance in poor weather or strong side winds.

questions.question: What happens to your view ahead when you leave a proper two-second gap?
options: You can see past the vehicle ahead and spot hazards earlier
You see less of the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 notes a wider gap improves your view of road hazards.

questions.question: Why could a late signal confuse other road users?
options: It gives them too little time to react safely
It breaks the speed limit rule
It turns off your brake lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses signalling early enough for others to read and react.

questions.question: Can you drive above the speed limit briefly while overtaking?
options: Yes, for up to five seconds
No, you must never exceed the speed limit
Yes, if no cameras are nearby
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 makes clear that speed limits are the legal maximum at all times.

questions.question: When the light changes from red and amber to green, what should you check before moving?
options: That the junction is clear of late crossers and pedestrians
questions.explain: Rule 175: green means you may go on if the way is clear; watch for late crossers.

questions.question: What if a pedestrian is waiting to cross the side road you are turning into?
options: Give way and let them cross safely
Wave them back and turn fast
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 170 and Rule 172 require giving way to pedestrians crossing side roads.

questions.question: Before stopping to let a pedestrian cross a side road you are turning into, what should you check?
options: Your mirrors so you brake safely
questions.explain: Rule H2: check your mirrors early so you can slow down smoothly without surprising traffic behind.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes without checking your blind spot?
options: You could hit a cyclist, rider, or car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 highlights that motorcycles and cars can hide in blind spots.

questions.question: Why should you not hug the centre line on a bend?
options: An oncoming vehicle could hit you
It is illegal to steer left
questions.explain: Rule 160: keeping left gives oncoming traffic room, especially where you cannot see round a bend.

questions.question: What should you also watch for before entering a roundabout besides cars?
options: Cyclists, motorcyclists, and pedestrians crossing the exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds drivers to watch out for cyclists, riders, and pedestrians.

questions.question: Which signal do you give on approach when going straight ahead (second exit)?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states not to signal on approach when going straight ahead.

questions.question: When taking the first exit to the left, what happens to your left signal?
options: Keep signalling left all the way around into the exit
Cancel it at the give-way line
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps the left signal on from approach through the first exit.

questions.question: At a double mini-roundabout, how do you pass each painted white circle?
options: Go clockwise around each mini-roundabout in turn
Cut straight across the second one anti-clockwise
Drive over the centre of both
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 require treating each mini-roundabout separately and passing clockwise.

questions.question: Before moving off on green at an ASL, where should you check for cyclists?
options: Your nearside mirror and blind spot, and ahead
questions.explain: Rule 178: check both ahead and to your left in case a cyclist is moving alongside you.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing blue lights comes behind you while you wait at a red light. Should you cross the red line?
options: Yes, always run the red light
No, do not break the law by crossing the red line
questions.explain: Rule 219: make room safely if you can without crossing the stop line on red or mounting the kerb.

questions.question: When two exit lanes merge after a roundabout, how should you leave?
options: Stay in your exit lane cleanly, then merge smoothly when safe
Squeeze both cars side by side into one lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps exits orderly until lanes merge safely downstream.

questions.question: Why do some large roundabouts paint route numbers like 'M6' inside the approach lanes?
options: To help you pick the right lane early for your destination
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide drivers cleanly through big junctions.

questions.question: Which turning direction has the special exception to wait inside a yellow box junction?
options: Turning right (when only oncoming traffic stops you)
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 grants the exception only for right turns blocked by oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Approaching a blind hill crest behind a slow cyclist, what should you do?
options: Wait behind until you can see the oncoming road is clear
Overtake on the blind crest anyway
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and Rule 166 forbid overtaking where you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: Why is two seconds still too short behind a vehicle on a wet road?
options: Wet roads double stopping distance, so leave at least four seconds
Brakes lock faster in dry weather
Two seconds only applies to bikes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 says to double the gap to four seconds in wet weather.

questions.question: What should you check before cancelling a signal early if you change your mind?
options: That nobody has already reacted to your first signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses clear, unambiguous signals at all times.

questions.question: What happens when variable gantry signs show a speed inside a red ring on a motorway?
options: That lower limit is legally enforced
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 and 258 make red-ring gantry limits legally binding.

questions.question: If a main road has two lanes in one direction and you turn left onto it, which lane should you join?
options: The left-hand lane unless road signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 and lane rules keep turning traffic in the left lane when clear.

questions.question: You see a motorcycle filtering between lanes as you plan to move right. What should you do?
options: Steer right anyway because you are bigger
Hold your lane and wait until the rider has passed safely
Open your door to warn them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires watching for motorcyclists before changing lanes.

questions.question: A lorry on the roundabout is taking the next exit, blocking your view of the lane behind it. What should you do?
options: Wait until the lorry clears so you can see any hidden vehicles behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 warns not to enter when a large vehicle hides traffic to your right.
